item.title: [LU-20888] DNE MDT recovery hangs if MDS_CONNECT finds a thread pool fully blocked on osp_remote_sync
item.description: When an MDT restarts while a peer MDT (MDT0000) is serving lookups for objects that live on the restarting MDT, MDT0000's regular mdt service threads all block in osp_remote_sync waiting on the restarting MDT. The restarting MDT's recovery then needs MDT0000 to accept its LWP MDS_CONNECT. That connect arrives with no export, so it is a normal-priority request, and the pool will not give it one of the threads reserved for high-priority work. It never gets serviced, the LWP never reaches FULL, FLD lookups can never be sent, and recovery waits forever.
item.summary: DNE MDT recovery hangs if MDS_CONNECT finds a thread pool fully blocked on osp_remote_sync

status.description: The issue is open and ready for the assignee to start work on it.

We saw a similar problem during recovery. A clients connection should be high priority too, not only LWP. I've pushed a common solution for connections. 

Summary

On an MDS hosting several DNE targets, a failover can produce a self-sustaining
deadlock between the ptlrpc service threads and target recovery:

  • mdt service threads block inside rename/getattr handlers waiting on
    cross-MDT OSP RPCs to a target that is itself still in recovery;
  • a recovering target cannot answer MDS_CONNECT because every thread in the
    affected CPT partition is blocked;
  • the target therefore never completes recovery, so the blocked threads are
    never released.

The cycle breaks only when the recovery soft timer expires and evicts the
clients that were waiting. The connects were delivered — they sat in the
service queue and were dropped unanswered, 157s past their own deadline.

Environment

  • Lustre 2.16 (cray), DNE, 4 MDTs, HA pairs.
  • MDS: 64 cores / 4 NUMA nodes / npartitions: 8 -> 8 CPTs, 100 mdt threads per CPT.
  • Clients on gni, servers on o2ib61, reached through LNet routers (routed traffic).
  • Reproducer: MDS panic/failover loop. After the peer panicked, all four MDTs
    ended up on one node.

The cycle

  1. MDT0000/MDT0002 fail over onto the node already hosting MDT0001/MDT0003.
  2. MDT0001/MDT0003 threads, handling ordinary client renames/getattrs, block in
    ptlrpc_queue_wait() on OSP RPCs to MDT0000/MDT0002.
  3. Those threads are mdt service threads that arrived on
    MDS_REQUEST_PORTAL — while blocked they still count in
    scp_nreqs_active.
  4. MDT0002's clients send MDS_CONNECT on the same portal, into the same CPT
    partition. No thread is free.
  5. MDT0002 cannot finish recovery (clients never connect); the threads cannot
    unblock (MDT0002 has not finished recovery).
  6. At the 300s soft timeout the stale sweep evicts 6 clients, which releases the
    threads — and one second later the queued connects are dequeued and dropped.

Evidence: the connect was delivered, queued, and dropped unanswered

Client 31@gni sends the connect at 1791896049 (T+44 of a 300s window):

00000100:00100000:58.0:1791896049.237153:0:17100:0:(import.c:814:ptlrpc_connect_import_locked())
  @@@ (re)connect request (timeout 5) req@... x1878873257675392/t0(0)
  o38->e2kp1-MDT0002-mdc-...@10.10.100.5@o2ib61

and gives up 41s later with -110:

(client.c:2383:ptlrpc_expire_one_request()) @@@ Request sent has timed out for slow reply:
  [sent 1791896049/real 1791896049] req@... x1878873257675392/t0(0) o38->e2kp1-MDT0002-...
(client.c:2414:ptlrpc_expire_one_request()) @@@ err -110, sent_state=CONNECTING (now=CONNECTING)

The server had the same xid the whole time. It is dequeued at
1791896306 — 257s after arrival, 157s past its own AT deadline — and
dropped without a reply:

Oct 13 07:58:26 LustreError: 221574:0:(service.c:2587:ptlrpc_server_handle_request())
  @@@ Dropping timed-out request from 12345-31@gni: deadline 100/157s ago
  req@... x1878873257675392/t0(0) o38-><?>@<unknown>:0/0 lens 520/0 e 0 to 0
  dl 1791896149 ref 1 fl Interpret:/200/ffffffff rc 0/-1

This message is emitted at dequeue, so it is positive proof the RPC arrived
and was queued — this is not packet loss and not an LNet routing problem.
Skipped 11 previous similar messages accompanies it.

Evidence: one CPT partition was fully drained

The blocked threads are in cross-MDT RPCs:

Lustre: mdt_io06_002: service thread pid 50292 was inactive for 200.960 seconds
  ptlrpc_set_wait <- ptlrpc_queue_wait <- osp_remote_sync <- osp_xattr_get
  <- lod_xattr_get <- __mdd_links_read <- mdd_is_subdir
  <- mdt_rename_determine_lock_order <- mdt_reint_rename

Lustre: mdt02_010: service thread pid 57553 was inactive for 200.177 seconds
  lu_object_find_at <- mdt_object_find <- mdt_getattr_name_lock
  <- mdt_intent_getattr <- mdt_intent_policy <- tgt_enqueue

At the instant the sweep releases them, 100 mdt threads report
completed after ~258s, and they are almost all in one partition:

CPT threads stalled
1 4
2 3
3 1
4 98
6 1

CPT 4 ran from mdt04_000 to mdt04_099 — its full 100-thread limit. 21
threads pre-existed; 77 were spawned during the stall (contiguous pids
221551-221740) and blocked as well. The other seven partitions were healthy
throughout.

Why only these clients: the CPT is a function of the client NID

With the default portal_rotor = LNET_PTL_ROTOR_HASH_RT
(lnet/lnet/lib-ptl.c:17), a routed request is assigned
cpt = lnet_nid2cpt(&msg->msg_initiator, ni) (lib-ptl.c:291-306,
lib-move.c:4493) — a hash of the originating client NID, not the router. For
non-KFI NIDs this is (sum of the 8 bytes of the nid64) mod ncpt
(api-ni.c:1656-1679), i.e. for gni with 8 CPTs: CPT = (13 + addr) mod 8.

The six evicted clients were 23, 31, 47, 55, 135, 151 @gni — every one
addr = 7 (mod 8), i.e. all six hash to CPT 4. No client outside that
residue class was evicted. This is a deterministic cohort, not an unlucky tail,
and it will recur on the same 1/8 of the cluster every time.
